name: Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services visa (技術・人文知識・国際業務)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a confirmed job offer from a Japanese employer for a role matching your qualification field (engineering/technical, humanities/business, or international/cross-cultural work).
This requires a university degree (or Japanese vocational college diploma) relevant to the role, or at least 10 years of relevant professional experience (3 years for international-services roles).
requirements.fix_path: Obtain qualification recognition or document sufficient relevant experience.

evidence_required.document: Degree certificate or documented equivalent professional experience

outcome.duration_length: 3 months, 1 year, 3 years, or 5 years, renewable

sources.title: Immigration Services Agency of Japan — 技術・人文知識・国際業務 (Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services) visa

notes: Japan's direct equivalent to UK Skilled Worker, Germany's general work permit, or NL Highly Skilled Migrant — the standard employer-sponsored office/technical/specialist route, and by volume the most commonly used work visa in Japan. No fixed salary threshold the way most European equivalents have (UK's £41,700, Germany's Blue Card formula) — Japanese immigration law instead requires that the salary be 'equal to or greater than that of a Japanese national performing the same duties,' a comparative rather than absolute test, genuinely different in kind from every salary-threshold route in the rest of this dataset; not encoded as a numeric requirement here since there's no single figure to cite. family_can_work is false — dependants hold 'Dependent' status with restricted part-time work only via separate permission, a real structural difference from most European family_can_work:true defaults in this dataset. pr_after_months (120) reflects Japan's genuinely long standard 10-year path — one of the longest standard PR timelines in this entire multi-country dataset, though citizenship_after_months (60) is shorter since Japan's naturalisation residence requirement (5 years) doesn't require holding PR first, unlike most European countries in this dataset where naturalisation is gated behind PR.
